Re: First-Level Medical Necessity Appeal  
Member: Jordan Iverson  
Member ID: W979574719  
Reference number: POC-E6EF62D505-92473  
Denied service: Lumbar decompression/discectomy  
CPT: 63030  
Date of denial notice: August 20, 2026

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/discectomy. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that UnitedHealthcare/Oxford overturn the denial and authorize the surgery.

The clinical records establish a persistent, progressive, structurally documented nerve-compression condition that has not responded adequately to appropriate conservative treatment:

- I have had progressive lower-back pain for nine months, despite rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility treatment, from April 17, 2026, through June 26, 2026. The physical-therapy discharge note documents 16 completed visits.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 2, 2026, provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- The June 17, 2026, lumbar MRI shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral-recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain extending into the right calf and cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

These records demonstrate a consistent match between the symptoms, examination findings, MRI abnormality, and affected nerve root. They also document substantial functional impairment and failure of medication, injection therapy, and a full supervised physical-therapy course. The requested procedure is directed at the identified L4-L5 disc extrusion and severe stenosis causing L5 nerve-root compression.

The records also do not identify clinical factors that would independently prevent surgery. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The treating surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has requested the procedure based on the documented structural compression, corresponding neurologic findings, persistent radicular symptoms, and failure of conservative treatment. Please have the surgeon’s complete prior-authorization submission and all attached clinical records reviewed by a physician qualified in spine surgery or orthopedic surgery.

The public UnitedHealthcare commercial policy identified for this request is Spinal Fusion and Decompression, policy 2026T0639I, effective April 1, 2026. That policy directs reviewers to InterQual lumbar decompression criteria. The detailed InterQual criteria were not reproduced in the publicly available policy document I reviewed, so I have not quoted plan language here. Please provide the exact InterQual criteria and version used in this denial, identify which specific criterion was found unmet, and explain how the documented MRI findings, neurologic deficit, functional limitations, and failed conservative treatment failed to satisfy that criterion.

Please reconsider the denial based on the enclosed records and authorize CPT 63030. If the denial is upheld, please provide the specific clinical basis, the exact criteria applied, the InterQual version used, and the qualifications of the reviewing clinician.

This appeal is submitted within the deadline stated in the denial notice, February 16, 2027.

Sincerely,

Jordan Iverson  
Member ID: W979574719
